sections.h2: How does property tax work in Johnson County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Johnson County property is valued by the county Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) as of January 1, billed and collected by the Johnson County Sheriff, and recorded through the Johnson County Clerk. Each of those offices does one piece of the job, so a question about value, a payment or a lien goes to a different desk.

Johnson County sits in the Eastern Coalfield, covers about 262 square miles of land and has Paintsville as its only city and county seat. The county government's main offices share an address at 230 Court Street in Paintsville. The county clerk is in Suite 124 at (606) 789-2557, open Monday through Friday from 8 AM to 4 PM, and the sheriff's office lists (606) 789-3411 with the same hours.

Rates are set by the taxing districts, not by the PVA. The Fiscal Court meets on the second Monday of the month at 4:45 PM, and the county has two public school districts, Johnson County Schools and Paintsville Independent, which are among the bodies whose levies make up a bill.

sections.h2: What does the Johnson County property tax calendar look like?
sections.html:
The assessment side of the calendar is fixed by state law, and the same dates apply in Johnson County as everywhere in Kentucky. The big one for homeowners is the thirteen-day inspection window that opens on the first Monday in May.

Kentucky property tax calendar steps that apply to Johnson County
StepTiming
Assessment dateJanuary 1
Real property listing periodJanuary 1 to March 1
Public inspection of the tax roll and PVA conferences13 days from the first Monday in May, Saturdays included
File an appeal with the county clerkOne workday after inspection closes
Board of Assessment AppealsFive days, starting 25 to 35 days after inspection
Personal property listingJanuary 1 to May 15

Source: Kentucky Department of Revenue, The Property Tax Calendar.

Bills are then mailed in the fall and paid to the sheriff. The standard Kentucky pattern is a 2 percent discount through November 1, face amount from November 2 to December 31, a 5 percent penalty in January, and a larger penalty plus a sheriff's fee from February 1. Ask the Johnson County Sheriff to confirm the exact dates for the current year.

sections.h2: What happens to a Johnson County tax bill that is not paid?
sections.html:
At the close of business on April 15, unpaid bills move from the sheriff to the Johnson County Clerk, and a lien is recorded against the property. From that point the cost grows quickly and the bill can be sold to a private buyer.

The Kentucky Department of Revenue explains the sequence. Interest at 1 percent per month starts when the clerk receives the bill, the county attorney's office mails notices, and the clerk advertises the delinquent list 30 to 45 days before a sale. State law puts the sale between 90 and 135 days after the transfer. Counties that also hold delinquent oil and gas or unmined mineral bills get an extra 60 days, which matters in a coalfield county where those interests are often billed apart from the surface.

  • The lien stays with the parcel, not the person.
  • If a third party buys the bill, you pay that buyer plus its fees.
  • Notices go by regular mail, so keep the PVA's address for you current.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Johnson County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with a conference at the Johnson County PVA office during the May inspection window, because Kentucky does not let you file with the board until that conference has happened. The PVA must explain how your value was reached, and a written record of the meeting is kept.

If you still disagree, file an appeal with the county clerk by the end of the workday after the inspection period closes. A local board of property owners hears it, and the clerk's office serves as the board's clerk. Without factual evidence, such as insurance policies, construction costs, sales listings or the physical characteristics of the land and buildings, the board must deny the appeal.

  • Ask the PVA for the sales it used to value your house.
  • Bring repair estimates if the home has damage the record does not show.
  • If someone is paid to speak for you, Kentucky limits who qualifies, including attorneys, certified public accountants and licensed appraisers.

A further appeal goes to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals. In a county where median values are modest, even a small dollar change can matter to a household budget, so it is worth the one phone call.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for exemptions in Johnson County?
sections.html:
Homeowners 65 or older, and owners who are totally disabled under a federal or retirement system program, can claim the homestead and disability exemption. The Department of Revenue says only one exemption is allowed per household and that it follows the owner, so a buyer has to apply on their own.

The exemption subtracts a set amount from assessed value, and the state adjusts it every two years. One county PVA's 2025 to 2026 announcement lists $49,100, but ask the Johnson County PVA to confirm the amount that applies to your bill. Totally disabled veterans and people found disabled under Social Security or Kentucky Retirement System rules do not need to reapply each year.

Churches, schools and charities apply on Revenue Form 62A023, and farm land is valued at its agricultural use, which the state says can mean sizable savings where market and farm values differ. Johnson County also has a county occupational tax of 0.5 percent of wages and net profit earned in the county, which is separate from property tax.

sections.h2: How does the Johnson County housing market affect the tax picture?
sections.html:
Values are lower and the population is older than in most of Kentucky. The Census Bureau puts the median owner-occupied home value at $120,200 for 2020 to 2024, the median household income at $44,904, and the population estimate for July 2025 at 22,051, down 2.8 percent from 2020.

The county has 10,714 housing units and a 68.3 percent owner-occupancy rate. The population peaked at 25,771 in 1940 and has drifted down since 1980. The 2020 census counted 12.0 percent of housing units as vacant, against 5.8 percent in Jessamine County and 6.9 percent in Kenton County.

Flood rules also matter for a seller. The county requires both a state and a local floodplain permit for construction in the Special Flood Hazard Area, and the county's floodplain page asks owners to call (606) 789-2550 before any development.

sections.h2: What should a Johnson County seller settle about taxes before closing?
sections.html:
Ask the sheriff for the current bill and a payoff, ask the clerk whether any certificate of delinquency exists on the parcel, and confirm the owner's exemption status with the PVA. Those three calls cover nearly every tax surprise at the closing table.

The county lists separate fire and rescue departments for Paintsville, Van Lear, West Van Lear and several other communities. A Kentucky bill can combine school, city, county and fire district levies, so ask the sheriff for the line-by-line breakdown. The Kenton County Sheriff notes that the seller's share of the year's tax is settled with the buyer at closing and the owner of record then pays the whole bill.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Johnson County, Kentucky?
faqs.a: The Johnson County Sheriff collects it. The sheriff's office lists (606) 789-3411 and is open Monday through Friday from 8 AM to 4 PM.

faqs.q: Where do I file a property tax appeal in Johnson County?
faqs.a: With the Johnson County Clerk at 230 Court Street, Suite 124, in Paintsville, after you hold the required conference with the PVA. The filing deadline is one workday after the May inspection period ends.

faqs.q: When does Johnson County send unpaid property tax to the clerk?
faqs.a: At the close of business on April 15. The Johnson County Clerk then holds the bill as a certificate of delinquency with a recorded lien.

faqs.q: Is the Johnson County homestead exemption automatic?
faqs.a: No. You apply through the PVA, you must be 65 or older and live in the home, and only one exemption is allowed per household.

faqs.q: Does the PVA set my Johnson County tax rate?
faqs.a: No. The PVA values property. Rates are set by the taxing districts such as the fiscal court and the school districts, and the sheriff collects the bill.
